pages.title: File:Corner of Freeland and Queen's Quay East -- streetcars are supposed to emerge from a tunnel here -a.jpg

ObjectName.value: Corner of Freeland and Queen's Quay East -- streetcars are supposed to emerge from a tunnel here -a

Categories.value: Redpath Sugar refinery|Queens Quay, Toronto|Self-published work|PD-self|Construction in Toronto|Freeland Street, Toronto|Panoramics of Toronto, 2012

ImageDescription.value:
Corner of Freeland and Queen's Quay East -- streetcars are supposed to emerge from a tunnel here.

There are big plans for this corner. Queen's Quay is now a four lane wide arterial road. It is to be reduced to two lanes. With a separate streetcar right of way along the south side, and with better pedestrian and cycle paths, also on the south side.

The Queen's Quay East streetcar line is supposed to run underground, for a couple of hundred metres, emerging at Freeland. The Queen's Quay West line emerges right after the line reaches Queen's Quay, and another emergence too close would disrupt traffic.

Toronto is scheduled to host the 2015 Pan American games. Currently there has been talk of building housing for visiting atheletes at the corner of Queen's Quay and Parliament. The streetcar line is initially to terminate at a loop just east of that intersection. At some future date the streetcar may run north, along Cherry Street, serving the distillery district, and a large new development east of there.

There has also been talk of sending the line south, along Cherry Street, to service the currently underutilized port lands.
